mainTopic: Washing hands: the dangers of skipping it, which water may be used, why we wash before bread, and washing before fruit
overview: This amud opens by finishing a story about a שד and the household of רב פפא, who poured off water from the pitcher before drinking. Then רב דימי and רבין each tell how skipping מים ראשונים and מים אחרונים once led to disaster. רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a memory trick for their two versions, and רבי אבא teaches the harsher story of each. Next, חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about washing hands with water heated by fire and with the hot springs of טבריא. רב פפא explains that their real dispute is about water led into a ditch, and the גמרא finds the same dispute among תנאים. The גמרא then gives the reasons for washing before bread: a safeguard for תרומה, and a מצוה hinted at in a פסוק about a זב. Washing before fruit turns out to be only for cleanliness. A story about רבי אמי and רבי אסי teaches rules about fruit, זימון, and two people who ate together. The amud ends as a ברייתא begins to give how much of the hand must be washed, and the rule continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The demon sees the household pour off water from the pitcher
steps.stepSummary: The story ends: the שד sees the household of רב פפא pouring water out of the pitcher's mouth and says it would not have delayed had it known.
steps.simpleTranslation: The demon saw them pouring water from the mouth of the pitcher. It said: If I had known you usually do this, I would not have held back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that began earlier. The שד sees the people pour some water off the top of the pitcher before drinking, and it comments on what it sees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The household had a habit of pouring off the first bit of water before drinking. The שד says that if it had known about this habit, it would not have held back, because it would have known they were going to pour that water off anyway. The story shows that this habit is a real form of protection.

keyTerms.meaning: mouth (here: the opening of the pitcher)
I would have held back / delayed

steps.whatToRemember: Pouring off a little water from the mouth of the pitcher before drinking is shown here as a protective habit.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a story that started before this section. 'It' and 'them' refer to the שד and the household of רב פפא from the earlier part of the story.

phrases.english: It saw them that they were pouring out water
phrases.notes: 'It' is the שד from the story that started before this line, and 'them' is the household of רב פפא.

phrases.english: from the mouth of the pitcher,
It said: If I had known
that you are accustomed to do this,
I would not have delayed.

steps.triggerLanguage: חזנהו דקא שדו מיא מפומא דחצבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The habit of pouring off water from the mouth of the pitcher protects against harmful water.

steps.title: רב דימי's report: the dangers of skipping the washings
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that skipping מים ראשונים led to someone being fed pig meat, and skipping מים אחרונים led to a woman being divorced from her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: The first waters caused someone to be fed pig meat. The final waters caused a woman to be sent away from her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רב דימי, arriving from ארץ ישראל, teaches that skipping the hand-washings before and after a meal once caused real disasters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is not that the water itself caused harm. Not washing set off a chain of events. Skipping the washing before eating made a Jew look like a non-Jew, so he was served pig meat. Skipping the washing after eating left signs of the meal on a man, and that led in the end to his wife being divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: the 'first waters': washing hands before the meal
the 'final waters': washing after the meal
caused a woman to leave her husband (she was divorced)

steps.confusionAlert: The words say the waters 'fed' and 'divorced,' but the meaning is that NOT washing led to these results.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching shows how seriously חז"ל took both מים ראשונים and מים אחרונים.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought teachings with him.

phrases.english: The first waters
phrases.notes: He means skipping the washing before the meal.

phrases.english: fed pig meat,
the final waters caused to go out
a woman from her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skipping מים ראשונים led to eating pig meat. Skipping מים אחרונים led to a divorce.

steps.title: Ravin's different version of the same teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports the teaching differently: skipping מים ראשונים led to eating נבלה, and skipping מים אחרונים led to a killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: The first waters caused someone to be fed carcass meat. The final waters killed a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same teaching, from רבין, who also came from ארץ ישראל. His details are different from רב דימי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages agree that skipping each washing led to a disaster, but they differ on the details. For the first waters, רבין says the meat was נבלה instead of pig meat. For the final waters, he says the result was even worse: the wife was killed, not just divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: meat of an animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
The first waters fed carcass meat,
the final waters killed a person.
phrases.notes: In his version, the husband killed his wife instead of divorcing her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב דימי's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skipping מים ראשונים led to eating נבלה. Skipping מים אחרונים led to a killing.

steps.title: A memory trick for the two versions
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a memory trick: רב דימי 'divorced her,' and רבין 'killed her.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Your memory sign is: רב דימי came and sent her out; רבין came and killed her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a short memory trick so we don't mix up which sage said which version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions are close, so it is easy to confuse them. The trick links each name to what happened to the wife: רב דימי's version has divorce, and רבין's version has killing. Once you remember that, you also remember that רב דימי said pig meat and רבין said נבלה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב דימי: pig meat and divorce. רבין: נבלה and killing. Memory sign: רב דימי 'sent her out,' רבין 'killed her.'

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
And your memory sign is:
Rav Dimi came and sent her out,
Ravin came and killed her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב נחמן בר יצחק וסימניך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a way to remember the two versions from steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Memory sign: רב דימי's version has divorce, and רבין's version has killing.

steps.title: רבי אבא teaches the stricter version of each story
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא takes one story from רב דימי's version and one from רבין's version, choosing the stricter one each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא would teach one story from this version and one story from that version, choosing the stricter one each time.
steps.whatsHappening: A third teacher, רבי אבא, mixes the two earlier versions. From each pair he picks the more severe story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי and רבין told different results for skipping each washing. רבי אבא does not choose one teacher's whole version. For each washing he takes the harsher outcome: for מים ראשונים, eating pig meat (רב דימי's version), and for מים אחרונים, a killing (רבין's version).
steps.whatToRemember: The stories end with רבי אבא's mix. Skipping מים ראשונים led to eating pig meat, and skipping מים אחרונים led to a killing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba would teach one from these
phrases.notes: He means one story from רב דימי's version, the one about pig meat for מים ראשונים.

phrases.english: and one from those, for the stricter side.
phrases.notes: And one story from רבין's version, the killing for מים אחרונים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא מַתְנֵי חֲדָא מֵהָנֵי, וַחֲדָא מֵהָנֵי, לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third way of teaching the stories from steps 2-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teach the harsher outcome for each washing: pig meat for מים ראשונים, and a killing for מים אחרונים.

steps.title: Can you wash hands with water heated by fire?
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says no; רבי יוחנן says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about water heated by fire: חזקיה says we do not wash hands with it, and רבי יוחנן says we do wash hands with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It records a dispute about using fire-heated water for washing hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether heating the water by fire makes it unfit for washing hands before eating. חזקיה forbids it and רבי יוחנן allows it. No reasons are given yet.

phrases.english: It was stated: water heated by fire —

phrases.aramaic: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר אֵין נוֹטְלִים מֵהֶן לַיָּדַיִם,
phrases.english: Hizkiyya says: we do not wash hands with it,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר נוֹטְלִין מֵהֶם לַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan says: we do wash hands with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic connected to washing hands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: חזקיה forbids washing with fire-heated water, and רבי יוחנן permits it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן brings support from the great sages of the גליל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asked רבן גמליאל, the son of רבי, who said all the great men of the גליל wash with heated water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: I asked רבן גמליאל, the son of רבי, who ate food in a state of purity, and he told me that all the great men of the גליל do this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן backs up his view with a report of what great sages actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The support is strong because רבן גמליאל ate his food in purity, so he would be very careful about washing hands. If he and the great men of the גליל washed with heated water, it must be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who eats his food in a state of ritual purity
The great sages of the גליל

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: I asked Rabban Gamliel,
the son of Rabbi, who ate food in purity,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לִי כׇּל גְּדוֹלֵי גָּלִיל עוֹשִׂין כֵּן.
phrases.english: and he said to me: all the great men of the Galilee do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's side of step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that fire-heated water may be used for washing hands
steps.raayaSupportSource: What רבן גמליאל and the great men of the גליל actually did

steps.title: The hot springs of טבריא
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says no pouring onto the hands, but you may dip the hands in the springs; רבי יוחנן says the whole body may be immersed, but not the face, hands and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the hot springs of טבריא, חזקיה says: we do not wash hands with them, but we may dip the hands in them. רבי יוחנן says: a person may immerse his whole body in them, but not his face, hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: A second dispute between the same two sages, this time about the natural hot springs of טבריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה allows dipping the hands right into the springs, but not washing by pouring. רבי יוחנן allows immersing the whole body, yet seems to forbid dipping just the face, hands and feet. That second point sounds strange, and the next step asks about it.

keyTerms.meaning: The natural hot springs of טבריא

phrases.english: The hot springs of Tiberias: Hizkiyya says:
we do not wash hands with them,
but we may dip the hands in them.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כׇּל גּוּפוֹ טוֹבֵל בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says: he may immerse his whole body in them,
but not his face, hands and feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel second dispute between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה: no washing by pouring, but dipping the hands is allowed. רבי יוחנן: the whole body may be immersed, but not the face, hands and feet.

steps.title: If the whole body is allowed, surely the hands are too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: if the whole body may be immersed, how can the face, hands and feet be forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if he may immerse his whole body in them, shouldn't his face, hands and feet be allowed all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's statement, because it seems to contradict itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing the whole body is the bigger act, and the hands are part of the body. So it seems strange to allow the whole and forbid the part.

phrases.english: Now, if he may immerse his whole body in them,

phrases.aramaic: פָּנָיו יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: his face, hands and feet — not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא כׇּל גּוּפוֹ טוֹבֵל בָּהֶם, פָּנָיו יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's words in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement "but not his face, hands and feet"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the larger act (the whole body) is allowed, the smaller act (just the hands) should surely be allowed too.

steps.title: רב פפא: the dispute is only about water in a ditch
steps.stepSummary: Everyone allows dipping in the springs where they are, and everyone forbids taking the water in a vessel. They only argue about water channeled into a ditch: should we make a גזירה because of a vessel?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: In the springs themselves, everyone agrees it is permitted. Taking water from them in a vessel, everyone agrees it is forbidden. They disagree when the water was channeled off into a ditch. One sage holds we make a גזירה about the ditch because of the vessel, and the other holds we don't.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. He shows that the two sages are really arguing about one middle case: water drawn into a ditch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the dispute is moved to the ditch, the question goes away. The "face, hands and feet" that רבי יוחנן forbids refers to dipping them in a ditch, which looks like using a vessel. The one who forbids it makes a גזירה so people won't come to use a vessel. The other sage does not make that גזירה.
steps.confusionAlert: "מר... ומר" does not name the sages. By the flow of the sugya, the one who makes the גזירה is רבי יוחנן, since he forbids the hands, and חזקיה does not make it.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels for the springs of טבריא: in place, allowed; in a vessel, forbidden; in a ditch, disputed because of a גזירה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: in their place —
everyone agrees that it is permitted;
taking from them in a vessel —
everyone agrees that it is forbidden.
Where they disagree — when one channeled them off into a ditch:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר גָּזְרִינַן בַּת בִּירְתָּא אַטּוּ מָנָא,
phrases.english: one sage holds we decree against a ditch because of a vessel,
and the other sage holds we do not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בִּמְקוֹמָן דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9 by narrowing the case being argued about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the dispute to a specific case (the ditch)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן seemed to forbid dipping the hands straight into the springs while allowing the whole body.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the springs everyone allows it, and in a vessel everyone forbids it. רבי יוחנן's ban on the hands is about a ditch, because of a גזירה, so it does not contradict allowing the whole body.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a typical way the גמרא settles a dispute: both sides agree on the clear cases at either end, and argue only about a middle case where a גזירה might apply.

steps.title: The same argument appears in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the argument between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן is like an argument between תנאים about water too spoiled for an animal to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: water that became too bad even for an animal to drink is unfit for washing if it is in vessels, but fit if it is in the ground. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: even in the ground, a person may immerse his whole body in it, but not his face, hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the earlier argument about washing in such water already existed among the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says water in the ground is fully fit. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר allows the whole body but not the face, hands and feet. That is the same strange-sounding position the גמרא saw in רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים; the later argument matches an older one
The ground, water still attached to the earth

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between Tannaim:
phrases.notes: The argument between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן from the last few steps matches the one in this ברייתא.

phrases.english: Water that became unfit even for an animal to drink,
in vessels, it is unfit,
in the ground, it is fit.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Even in the ground,
one may immerse his whole body in it,
but not his face, hands and feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the argument explained in Step 10 already existed among the תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The argument between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן about spring water
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר

steps.title: How can the whole body be allowed but not the hands?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same logical question about רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that it asked about רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if he may immerse his whole body in it, then his hands and feet, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: if the whole body is allowed, the hands and feet should be allowed even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hands and feet are part of the whole body. So it makes no sense to allow the bigger thing and forbid the smaller thing. This is the same question as in Step 9, now asked about the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if this is so; opens an argument from logic

phrases.english: Now, if he may immerse his whole body in it,
his hands and feet, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the ברייתא from Step 11 the same question that Step 9 asked about רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the larger case, the whole body, is allowed, the smaller case, the hands and feet, should be allowed too.

steps.title: The argument is about water led into a ditch
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be talking about water channeled into a ditch, and the תנאים argue whether to make a גזירה because of a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be that he channeled the water into a ditch, and this is what they argue about: one master holds we make a גזירה on a ditch because of a vessel, and the other holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying the ברייתא is about water led into a ditch. That is exactly the case where חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water in a ditch is not in a vessel, but it looks a bit like it. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids washing hands there so people won't come to wash from a vessel. The תנא קמא does not worry about that. This finishes showing that the amoraic argument from Step 10 is the same as this one between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: A ditch or channel the water was led into
We make a גזירה, a protective rabbinic decree
Because of, out of concern for

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is only about water led into a ditch: should we forbid it because it might lead people to use water from a vessel? רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says yes, the תנא קמא says no.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that he channeled the water into a ditch,
and this is what they argue about:
that one master holds we make a decree
on a ditch because of a vessel,
phrases.notes: This first master is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. That is why he forbids the hands and feet.

phrases.english: and the other master holds we do not make a decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by limiting the ברייתא to the ditch case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (ditch water, not water in its natural place)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to be about water in the ground in general, which made it illogical.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is only about ditch water and whether to make a גזירה because of a vessel.

steps.title: Why we wash hands before ordinary food
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אשיאן teaches that washing hands for חולין is a safeguard for תרומה, and also a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן: washing hands before eating ordinary food is a safeguard because of תרומה. And also because it is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic and gives two reasons why חכמים required washing hands before eating ordinary food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים must wash before eating תרומה. If everyone washes before all food, the כהנים will stay in the habit. The second reason, 'a מצוה', is not explained yet, so the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: A related safeguard, something done because of a connection to another law
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said,
Rav Yitzchak bar Ashiyan said:
Washing hands for ordinary food
is because of a safeguard for תרומה.
And also because of a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין, אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַשְׁיָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the reason for washing hands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing hands for חולין is a safeguard for תרומה, and also a מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for why we wash hands before bread even though we do not eat תרומה.

steps.title: Which מצוה is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the 'מצוה' in the statement refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the second reason, which was left unexplained. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement said washing is 'also a מצוה' but did not say which one. The גמרא wants to know what that word means here.

keyTerms.meaning: A commandment, something one is told to do

phrases.english: What מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of the last words of Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the 'מצוה' of washing hands is.

steps.title: אביי: listening to חכמים
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the מצוה is to obey the words of חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is a מצוה to listen to the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the מצוה is simply obeying what חכמים instituted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's view, the מצוה is the general duty to follow חכמים. Since they made this rule, keeping it fulfills that duty.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a מצוה to listen to the words of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מצוה is obeying the words of חכמים.

steps.title: רבא: the hint in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the מצוה is to follow רבי אלעזר בן ערך, who found a hint for washing hands in a פסוק about a זב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is a מצוה to listen to the words of רבי אלעזר בן ערך, as it is written: 'And whoever the זב touches, without having rinsed his hands in water.' רבי אלעזר בן ערך said: from here the חכמים found a Torah support for washing hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer: washing hands has a hint in a פסוק, as רבי אלעזר בן ערך taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about a זב who did not rinse his hands, which suggests that rinsing hands matters. אביי sees the מצוה as obeying חכמים in general. רבא connects it to a specific source in the תורה that חכמים leaned on.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a discharge that makes him טמא

steps.whatToRemember: Washing hands for bread has two reasons: a safeguard for תרומה, and a מצוה. אביי says the מצוה is obeying חכמים. רבא says it is following רבי אלעזר בן ערך, who found a hint in a פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'מן התורה' here means the חכמים found a support in a פסוק for their rule. It does not mean that washing for bread is a full דאורייתא law.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מִצְוָה לִשְׁמוֹעַ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ,
phrases.english: It is a מצוה to listen to the words of Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh,
as it is written: 'And whoever the zav touches,'
'without having rinsed his hands in water.'
Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh said:
From here the Sages found support
for washing hands from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִצְוָה לִשְׁמוֹעַ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from אביי's in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מצוה is following רבי אלעזר בן ערך, who found a hint for washing hands in the פסוק about a זב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that חכמים connected washing hands to a hint in the תורה, not only to a safeguard.

steps.title: How does the פסוק about a זב hint at hand-washing?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן how the hint for נטילת ידים is drawn from the פסוק about a זב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: How is this shown?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks how רבי אלעזר בן ערך's hint, from the previous step, actually works. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the hint for washing hands comes from a פסוק about a זב. But a פסוק about a זב does not obviously talk about washing before a meal. רבא wants to see exactly how the words lead there.

keyTerms.meaning: What shows this? How is this implied by the words?

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:
From where is this implied?
phrases.notes: He means: how does the פסוק about a זב hint at washing hands, as רבי אלעזר בן ערך said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the source given in step 17 actually works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the words of the פסוק about a זב point to washing hands.

steps.title: The plain reading of the פסוק cannot be right
steps.stepSummary: Read plainly, the פסוק suggests that a זב who rinsed his hands is clean. That is impossible, because a זב needs a full טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he has not rinsed his hands in water.' That would mean that if he did rinse, he is clean? But a זב needs a full immersion!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains to רב נחמן by first reading the פסוק simply, and he shows that this reading gives an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק talks about a זב 'who has not rinsed his hands,' it sounds like rinsing would make him clean. But a זב needs טבילה, immersing his whole body. So the words cannot be about the זב himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersing the whole body in a מקוה
A man made טמא by a certain bodily discharge

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And he has not rinsed his hands in water,'
which implies that if he did rinse, he is pure?
But he needs immersion!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows why the simple reading of the פסוק cannot work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of 'וידיו לא שטף במים' as describing the זב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would make hand-rinsing enough to purify a זב, but a זב needs full טבילה.

steps.title: The פסוק is hinting at someone else who has not washed
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק really means: there is another person who, if he has not washed his hands, is treated as טמא. That is the hint for נטילת ידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: and another person who has not rinsed his hands is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his explanation by rereading the פסוק so that it no longer talks about the זב. It now hints at a different person, someone who must wash his hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'he has not rinsed his hands' are read as a separate idea about another person. Without washing, his hands count as טמא. This becomes the hint from the תורה for washing hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it is saying (a rereading)

steps.whatToRemember: The hint for נטילת ידים: 'one who has not rinsed his hands' is treated as טמא. It does not mean that a זב becomes clean by rinsing.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
And another person who has not rinsed his hands is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty by rereading the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק says a זב who rinsed his hands becomes clean.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק hints that another person, one who has not washed his hands, is טמא.

steps.title: Washing before fruit is only for cleanliness
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי אושעיא, teaches that washing hands before fruit was said only for cleanliness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: They only said to wash hands before fruit because of cleanliness.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: does one need to wash before eating fruit? רבי אושעיא says it is only about being clean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing before bread is a rule of the חכמים connected to טהרה. Washing before fruit is different. It has nothing to do with טומאה and is only about clean hands.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
They did not speak of washing hands for fruit
except because of cleanliness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from washing before bread to washing before fruit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing before fruit is only for cleanliness.

steps.title: People understood: not required, but still a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: People understood רבי אושעיא to mean that washing before fruit is not required, but it is still a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this: there is no obligation, but there is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The listeners draw a conclusion from רבי אושעיא's words. This sets up רבא's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing 'only for cleanliness,' people thought it was a lower level: not a חובה, but still a good deed. רבא is about to reject this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (a first impression that may be wrong)
A good deed one is encouraged to do

phrases.english: They understood from this:
it is an obligation that there is not,
but a מצוה there is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First impression: washing before fruit is a מצוה, though not a חובה.

steps.title: רבא: it is only optional
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the inference. Washing before fruit is neither a חובה nor a מצוה, only רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to them: Not an obligation and not a מצוה, but optional.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on how people understood רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Only for cleanliness' means it has no religious weight at all. Someone may wash if he likes, but there is no מצוה in it.

keyTerms.meaning: Optional, left up to the person

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with washing before bread, which is required. Here we are only talking about fruit.

phrases.english: Rava said to them:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא חוֹבָה וְלֹא מִצְוָה, אֶלָּא רְשׁוּת.
phrases.english: Not an obligation and not a מצוה, but optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that washing before fruit is a מצוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Only for cleanliness' leaves no מצוה at all; it is purely optional.

steps.title: רב נחמן disagrees: washing for fruit is arrogant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבא disagrees with רב נחמן, who says one who washes before fruit is among the arrogant.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רב נחמן, for רב נחמן said: One who washes his hands for fruit is nothing but one of the arrogant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a different opinion. רב נחמן says one should not wash for fruit at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said washing for fruit is optional and fine. רב נחמן says doing it is wrong, a show of haughtiness. So the two disagree.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Naḥman,
phrases.notes: It is רבא's view, that washing is fine but optional, that clashes with רב נחמן's view.

phrases.english: as Rav Naḥman said:
One who washes his hands for fruit
is nothing but one of the arrogant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבא's view conflicts with רב נחמן's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: washing before fruit is a sign of arrogance.

steps.title: The story of רבי אמי and רבי אסי eating fruit
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה describes how רבי אמי and רבי אסי ate fruit without washing, gave him none, and each said his own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: I was standing before רבי אמי and רבי אסי. They were brought a basket of fruit. They ate without washing their hands, gave me nothing, and each one said the ברכה by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about what two great sages did. The next step will draw rules from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three details matter: they did not wash, they did not include רבה בר בר חנה to make a third person, and they did not join together for the ברכה.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: I was standing before Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
they brought before them a basket of fruit,
and they ate and did not wash their hands,
and they did not give me anything,
and each one blessed by himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case about fruit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי and רבי אסי ate fruit without washing and each said his own ברכה.

steps.title: Three lessons from the story
steps.stepSummary: From the story we learn: no washing before fruit, no זימון on fruit, and two who ate should each say their own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from it: there is no washing hands for fruit; there is no זימון on fruit; and two who ate together should separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls three practical rules out of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not washing shows that washing is not needed for fruit. Not adding a third person shows that זימון does not apply to fruit. Each saying the ברכה alone shows that two people should not have one person say it for both.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a זימון, a group invitation before ברכת המזון
To separate, each saying his own ברכה

steps.whatToRemember: Fruit: no washing, no זימון. Two people who ate: each makes his own ברכה.

phrases.english: Learn three things from it:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אֵין נְטִילַת יָדַיִם לְפֵירוֹת,
phrases.english: learn from it that there is no washing of hands for fruit,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אֵין מְזַמְּנִין עַל הַפֵּירוֹת,
phrases.english: and learn from it that one does not make a zimmun over fruit,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ שְׁנַיִם שֶׁאָכְלוּ – מִצְוָה לֵיחָלֵק.
phrases.english: and learn from it that two who ate, it is a מצוה to separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws rules from the story in step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No washing and no זימון for fruit; two who ate should each bless separately.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports: two who ate should separate
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also teaches that two who ate together should each say their own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: two who ate, it is a מצוה to separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the third lesson from the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about two people is no longer based only on what two sages did. It is also stated directly in an older teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (support from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
Two who ate, it is a מצוה to separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the third lesson of step 26.
steps.raayaObject: Two who ate should each say their own ברכה.

steps.title: When one is learned and one is not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its rule: it applies only when both are learned. If one is not, the learned one says the ברכה and the other fulfills his duty by listening.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When both were learned. But if one is learned and one is unlearned, the learned one says the ברכה and the unlearned one fulfills his duty through him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds an exception to the rule that two should separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating only makes sense when each person can say the ברכה himself. If one cannot, the learned one says it aloud, and the other fulfills his obligation by listening.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (limits a rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule of separating has limits. Hearing a ברכה from someone else counts when a person cannot say it properly himself.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
When both of them were scribes,
phrases.notes: 'Scribes' here means learned people who know how to say the ברכה properly.

phrases.english: but if one is a scribe and one is unlearned,
the scribe blesses and the unlearned one fulfills his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets limits on the rule quoted in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two separate only if both are learned; otherwise the learned one says the ברכה for both.

steps.title: How much of the hand to wash: regular food versus תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that for חולין one washes until the joint of the fingers, and begins giving a different measure for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: washing hands for regular food goes until the joint. For תרומה (the rule continues next).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives a measure for how much of the hand must be washed. It gives the measure for חולין and starts the one for תרומה, which is completed in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about whether and when to wash. Now the ברייתא adds something new: how much of the hand must be washed. By setting חולין next to תרומה, it signals that the more holy food will need a larger area washed.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual washing of the hands before eating
A joint; here, the joint of the fingers
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which has stricter purity rules

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule for תרומה is missing. The sentence simply continues in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Washing of the hands for regular food —
is until the joint,
phrases.notes: He means the joint of the fingers. That is how far the water must reach for regular food.

phrases.english: for תרומה —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier discussion of when one washes, including the fruit story, to a new ברייתא about how much of the hand is washed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For חולין, washing must reach until the joint of the fingers. A separate measure is about to be given for תרומה.
